findings.title: Device-limit rejection is cached, allowing the rejected device on its next request
findings.body: tagDeviceUI inserts the device ID into localCache before calling CreateOrUpdateDevice and does not remove the entry when that call returns ErrDeviceLimitReached. The first request from a new device over the limit is rejected, but for the next 29 minutes TagDevice sees the cache entry and returns nil, so Anonymous.Authenticate succeeds for the same over-limit device. The cache should only be populated after a successful store write (or evicted on error).

findings.title: Device-limit check is a non-atomic count-then-insert race
findings.body: CreateOrUpdateDevice runs CountDevices in one DB session, drops back to application code, and then inserts in a separate session with no transaction, unique constraint enforcement, or inter-instance lock. Concurrent requests (including from multiple Grafana instances sharing one database) when the count is limit-1 can all observe count < limit and all insert, exceeding the configured limit. The count check and insert/update need to be atomic, e.g. performed in a single transaction with appropriate locking.

findings.title: Provider signature changes are not reflected in the generated Wire code
findings.body: ProvideAnonDBStore changed from (db.DB) to (db.DB, int64) and ProvideAnonymousDeviceService changed from accepting anonstore.AnonStore to db.DB, but no wire_gen.go/wire set file is updated in this PR. The checked-in generated server wiring still calls these providers with the old arguments, so the server package will not compile until wire is regenerated and the generated file is committed.

findings.title: No test covers an already-known device being allowed when the limit is reached
findings.body: TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit only verifies that a second, new device is rejected. It does not verify the other half of the new contract in updateDevice: that re-tagging the existing device while count >= limit succeeds and updates it, nor that an expired device is rejected. A regression in the UPDATE ... BETWEEN window or in dialect-specific RowsAffected handling would incorrectly lock out legitimate existing anonymous devices and would not be caught.

findings.title: New device_limit option is not declared in defaults/sample config or docs
findings.body: AnonymousDeviceLimit is read from auth.anonymous device_limit, but the PR adds no entry to conf/defaults.ini or conf/sample.ini and no documentation for [auth.anonymous] device_limit. Operators have no discoverable way to learn the option exists, its unit/scope (distinct devices seen in 30 days), or that 0 means unlimited, so the headline configurable feature is effectively undocumented.
